acceptance_rule.rule: Frame C.  A proposal that is legal, and whose Scope clause the tool could calibrate, enters the verification queue.  The replay over the units this arm has already processed is measured and reported, but it does not refuse the candidate: it orders the queue and it comes back to you as feedback.  Entering the queue is not acceptance and carries no deployment right -- the candidate is only offered to later units, Fast decides whether to probe or deploy it, and the Skill is patched only after an independent later unit passes the authoritative delayed gate.
acceptance_rule.queue_order: Queued candidates are ordered by, in this order: (1) the common-denominator utility difference against the parent over the units already processed, larger first; (2) fewer cells where the pair is confirmed not executable and falls back to raw, because a program that cannot run on the cells already seen is less likely to run on the next one; (3) the position it was proposed at, then the order the model returned it.  Every input is a reading on evidence that has already arrived; no later unit, no later face and no future score enters the key.

proposals.what_changes: Replaces the frozen outlier_mad program with the hampel_filter operator, which detects and corrects outliers via a local median-based window mechanism rather than a global MAD threshold.
proposals.expected_change: Should help the series that were damaged by outlier_mad (T108, T109, T115, T118) by using a more localized outlier correction that preserves underlying level structure, while retaining gains on the majority of treated series that have high local_robust_z_peak.

proposals.what_changes: Replaces outlier_mad with outlier_iqr, which uses the interquartile range to detect and correct outliers, a different mechanism from the MAD-based approach.
proposals.expected_change: Expected to reduce the harm seen on the losing series (T108, T109, T115, T118) by using quartile-based bounds rather than median-absolute-deviation bounds, which may be more appropriate for skewed series among the treated population.

hampel_filter({})>outlier_mad({}).what_changes: Adds hampel_filter as the first step, followed by the frozen outlier_mad step, without changing the serving scope. This two-operator sequence is effect-distinct from the single hampel proposal and may reduce the amount of damage done per treated series while keeping the aggregate improvement.

winsorize({})>hampel_filter({}).what_changes: Applies winsorize before hampel_filter, reversing the promoted draft's order. outlier_mad({})>winsorize({}).what_changes: Replaces the frozen program with outlier_mad followed by winsorize, a different operator order from all previously tried candidates (hampel->winsorize, winsorize->outlier_mad, etc.) that has not yet been replayed.

hampel_filter({})>denoise_median({}).what_changes: Replaces the frozen operator with a hampel filter followed by a median denoiser, a pipeline combining robust spike removal with smoothing that has a different effect geometry from winsorize/outlier_mad chains.
